title: OpenViking trial: index the docs for agents?
question: Should agents look things up through an OpenViking index of the docs, next to or instead of ripgrep?

options.label: adopt
options.note: Run it all the time (CPU embedder, about 6 GB RAM), add the read-only MCP server for Claude Code and Codex, and refresh the index after each commit, with summaries under the GPU lock. On 15 questions it answered 10 (reading the top 3 hits), against 12 for first-try ripgrep, at about the same total tokens.

options.label: don't
options.note: Keep docs/game/README.md and ripgrep. Everything stays in ~/ai/openviking, stopped; nothing in the repo uses it. The generated L0/L1 summaries describe files without the facts in them, and the index is one more copy that goes stale.

options.label: adopt with changes
options.note: Vectors only (no GPU, no summaries), the read-only search tool offered as an extra next to ripgrep for plain-language questions (where it found answers in 1 to 1.5k tokens that took ripgrep 10 to 12k), and a quick refresh (37 s) after each commit.

links.label: The trial: setup, numbers per question, cost

decision: don't adopt; focus on making our docs better instead
